claim: Peer-to-peer is fused off in the CMP SKU: nvidia-smi topo -p2p reports GNS ('GPU not supported') and torch.cuda.can_device_access_peer is False in both directions.
scope_conditions: 2x unlocked CMP 170HX in one box, both Gen2 x16, PHB topology, 2026-08-21
quoted_support: The cause is in nvidia-smi topo -p2p: GNS - GPU not supported. Peer-to-peer is fused off in the CMP SKU, not blocked by IOMMU or ACS, so nothing in BIOS or the kernel recovers it.

claim: Without P2P, device-to-device copies are host-staged at 5.85 GB/s, no faster than the 6.17 GB/s host-to-device path.
stance_target: The repo's claim that all inter-GPU traffic crosses the host bridge, so GPU-to-GPU bandwidth collapses to host bandwidth
quoted_support: device-to-device copies are host-staged at 5.85 GB/s (no faster than the 6.17 GB/s H2D), and vLLM logs it plainly: Custom allreduce is disabled because your platform lacks GPU P2P capability

claim: TP=2 on this fabric raises single-stream decode by 23% (57.5 to 70.9 tok/s) but drops 16-agent aggregate throughput by 32% (608 to 415 tok/s).
stance_target: The repo's claim that TP is not viable for throughput on this box
scope_conditions: 2x CMP 170HX, same engine/checkpoint/flags as the single-card 27B run, only --tensor-parallel-size changed

claim: TP=2 makes 48K-context prefill 75% slower (27.1 to 47.4 s), because allreduce payload grows with batch size and the penalty lands hardest where the second card was supposed to help.
stance_target: The repo's claim that TP costs scale with tokens and therefore get worse exactly at the large batches training needs
quoted_support: 48K prefill 27.1 -> 47.4 s (-75%) ... Allreduce payload scales with batch size, so the penalty grows exactly where you wanted the second card to help.

claim: PP=2 is 3.2x faster than TP=2 on 48K prefill (14.8 s vs 47.4 s) and reaches 895 tok/s at 32 agents where TP=2 could not scale at all.
stance_target: The repo's claim that pipeline parallel is the topology that survives this fabric
quoted_support: 48K prefill 14.8 s vs 47.4 s - 3.2x faster ... 32 agents 895 tok/s - TP=2 could not scale here at all

claim: Two independent TP=1 servers reach 1,253 tok/s at 32 agents versus 415 tok/s for TP=2, a 3.0x win on identical silicon.
stance_target: The repo's claim that data-parallel replicas beat tensor parallelism on this fabric
scope_conditions: 2x CMP 170HX, one TP=1 server per card behind a load balancer
quoted_support: If you are throughput-bound, do not use TP=2. Run one TP=1 server per card behind a load balancer: 1,253 tok/s vs 415, a 3.0x win on identical silicon.

claim: The TP=2 crossover is around 3 concurrent agents: below that TP wins on latency, above it TP loses on throughput.
stance_target: Whether TP is ever worth using on this box
quoted_support: TP=2 makes one stream faster and everything else slower. The crossover is around 3 agents.

claim: Measured PCIe x16 versus x4 gives host-to-device 6.63 versus 1.7 GB/s, and decode and prefill did not move at all.
stance_target: The repo's open question that a Gen2 x16 link would drop every communication cost ~4x and weaken the large-batch-only conclusion
scope_conditions: Same card and workload, link width changed from x4 to x16, inference workloads only
quoted_support: PCIe x16 vs x4: H2D 6.63 vs 1.7 GB/s. Decode and prefill did not move. Pay for the solder mod only if you care about load, KV restore, and vision H2D.

claim: The unlock maps an 8 GB SKU to 64 GB, while a 10 GB SKU reaches only ~40 GB stable rather than the advertised 80 GB.
stance_target: The repo's 64 GB-per-card claim, and the caveat that unlock results depend on the SKU
scope_conditions: cmpunlocker software unlock, verified by 65536 MiB reported and a compute microbench
quoted_support: Software unlock (cmpunlocker) - or a seller who already did it. Verify 65536 MiB and a compute microbench. 8 GB SKU -> 64 GB; 10 GB SKU -> ~40 GB stable, not 80 GB.

claim: Gen2 link speed is a software unlock while link width is a hardware mod requiring 24x 0402 AC-coupling capacitors.
stance_target: The repo's claim that the cmpunlocker link patch lifts the cards to Gen2 and that width is set by the slot/solder
quoted_support: Optional hardware: 24x 0402 AC-coupling capacitors for PCIe x16. Gen2 speed is software; width is solder

claim: PP=2 matches a single card's throughput (605 vs 608 tok/s) while holding 2.3x the KV pool, so PP buys capacity without a throughput tax.
stance_target: The repo's claim that PP is the right way to use the second and further cards
quoted_support: PP=2 matches a single card's throughput (605 vs 608 tok/s) while holding 2.3x the KV pool. That is the combination we wanted from the second card and failed to get from TP=2: full speed and the capacity.

claim: On a 72B model at TP=2, batch load drives power DOWN (304 W at 32 agents versus 437 W on one stream) because the cards idle on the host-staged allreduce instead of computing.
stance_target: The repo's claim that communication, not compute, becomes the bottleneck under load on this fabric
scope_conditions: Qwen2.5 72B AWQ at TP=2, 32K window, FP8 KV, 2x CMP 170HX
quoted_support: Power inverts what you would guess: 437 W median on one stream, 304 W at 32 agents - under batch the cards idle on the host-staged allreduce instead of computing.

claim: A 30B model at PP=2 reaches 1,103 tok/s at 32 agents with a 5.25M-token KV pool, but at 16 agents a single card is faster (790 vs 626 tok/s).
stance_target: Whether adding cards always helps, which bears on how many GPUs a training run should claim
scope_conditions: Muse Glimmer 30B W4A16, bf16 KV, dev-branch vLLM, 2x CMP 170HX
quoted_support: But note the row that does not flatter the second card: at 16 agents one card is faster (790 vs 626). The second card only pays off past ~16 concurrent agents, or when you want the deeper pool.
